newsitem.title: USA: Three large retailers report higher second quarter results.
newsitem.headline: Three large retailers report higher second quarter results.

text.p: Department store companies May Department Stores Co. and Nordstrom Inc. and specialty clothing chain Abercrombie & Fitch Co. all reported higher earnings for the second quarter Monday, bolstered by healthy consumer spending this summer.

The results reflected an upbeat outlook among consumers about the economy, strong sales during July and conservative management among retailers of inventory, which helped curb profit-eating markdowns, analysts said.
"As long as inventories remain lean and as long as employment stays strong, we should be in store for a pretty robust second half of the year," said Todd Slater of investment bank Lazard Freres & Co.
Nordstrom and Abercrombie & Fitch's earnings exceeded Wall Street estimates, while May Department Stores met estimates.

Nordstrom's net income rose 31 percent to $58.6 million, or 76 cents a share, during the second quarter, from $44.8 million, or 55 cents a share, in the same period last year. Wall Street analysts had expected earnings of 68 cents a share.
Seattle-based Nordstrom said sales improved at its women's clothing department, where sales had been disappointing and inventories swelled late last year and earlier this year.

The company, however, told analysts during a conference call Monday that sales of designer lines had been strong during the second quarter. While apparel inventories were higher, the increase included less expensive apparel that the company can get rid of more easily than designer goods, analysts said.
"We are encouraged by an increase in sales, better expense control and gross margin improvements," Nordstrom Chairman John Whitacre said in a statement.
"Our women's apparel departments continue to show steady gains. These departments performed particularly well during the recent Anniversary Sale."

Columbus, Ohio,-based Abercrombie & Fitch said earnings rose to $2.1 milion, or 4 cents a share, from $283,000, or 1 cent a share, in the second quarter of 1996. Sales rose 51 percent to $86.6 million from $57.4 million last year, and same-store sales were up 15 percent during the second quarter.
Wall Street analysts had expected the retailer's earnings per share to be flat at 1 cent. Abercrombie had 139 men's clothing stores at the end of the period.

May Department Stores, parent of Lord & Taylor, Foley's and Robinsons-May store chains, said its earnings rose 5 percent to $116 million, or 46 cents a share, from $110 million, or 41 cents a share, in the second quarter of last year.

The results were in line with analysts' estimates. Earnings per share rose more than net income, or by 12 percent, because the company has repurchased $900 million in stock since the second quarter of 1996.
St. Louis-based May's sales rose 10 percent to $2.67 billion from $2.4 billion in the year-ago period, and same-store sales were up 4.7 percent.
Retailers closed the books on the second quarter late last month.
Business was soft for many retailers early in the quarter. But since they kept their inventories light, they did not have to slash prices this year to get rid of goods.

"They're controlling their markdowns a lot better than we've seen over the last couple years," said Richard Church of brokerage Smith Barney. "They're really trying to keep their inventories in check."

Sales strengthened at many chains in late June and early July after hot weather stirred up demand for air conditioners, lawn and garden goods and summer clothing. But analysts said the warm weather could begin to work against retailers because consumers are more likely to buy fall goods when it's cool.
